text:
Alex (support): Hey team — ACME reported repeated 503s during a traffic surge this morning on their dedicated pool. They say instances were created but requests still 503. Investigating now.

autoscaler-bot: detected scale event: requested +8 nodes for pool: acme-prod-dedicated at 2024-11-16T09:12:23Z

Jordan (eng-runtime): grabbing logs from the attach service. Do we see failed mounts or image pulls?

Alex (support): quick summary from customer: 09:10 -> spike, 09:12 -> 503s, 09:15 -> ticket. They saw new instances show up in console but traffic didn't route.

Lina (eng-sre): I see nodes provisioning but pods never hit READY. Readiness checks keep failing with 401 from internal config fetch. Minimal crashloop.

DevOps: paste of pod log snippet: 
```
2024-11-16T09:13:10Z startup: fetching config from https://config.internal/acme -> 401 Unauthorized
2024-11-16T09:13:10Z startup: marking pod unready, retrying config fetch in 5s
2024-11-16T09:13:16Z liveness: all checks passed but readiness=false
```

Jordan (eng-runtime): interesting — the config fetch uses a customer-scoped secret (acme/config-api-key). If that secret is invalid the app stays unready. Why would secret be invalid on new nodes only?

Alex (support): Customer confirmed they rotated their config API key yesterday but we didn't roll that secret into the dedicated pool's mount path. Their on-cluster secret was stale.

Maya (customer-success): ACME is asking why autoscale didn't prevent outage if new nodes were added. They lost 12% of requests. They're pretty upset.

Lina (eng-sre): Root cause chain: new pods spun up -> init tries to fetch external config -> secret invalid -> readiness=false -> autoscaler sees pods unready and keeps spinning up until min/max cap is hit -> traffic continues hitting only old nodes which are saturated -> 503s. Also, our attach flow marked nodes as "attached" as soon as node provisioned, not when pods are Ready.

Jordan (eng-runtime): noted. We have two separate issues: (1) orchestration marks capacity available too early, and (2) lack of guardrail for repeated readiness failures due to secret mismatch. We should not mark pool capacity as healthy until probe-based readiness across N pods passes.

DevOps: repro steps I used locally: 
1) kubectl set env deployment/acme-service CONFIG_KEY=stalekey -n acme
2) scale deployment to 20 and watch readiness: kubectl get pods -w -n acme
3) curl <route> returns 503 while new pods are Creating/CrashLoop

Jordan (eng-runtime): quick patch idea: change attach state machine to require at least 2/3 of newly-created pods Ready before reporting capacity to routing layer. Also add a counter for identical readiness failures per-pool that fires an alert.

Lina (eng-sre): agree. Also add a diagnostic in console showing "recent readiness error classes" (e.g., 401-config-fetch, image-pull, mount-failure) so SEs can triage faster.

Alex (support): For ACME right now — temporary mitigation: we can mark old nodes as warm-only and route traffic to them while CS rolls the secret back or updates the cluster secret. Or we can force a rolling restart after they provision correct secret. Which is faster?

Maya (customer-success): ACME can update the secret; they asked us to hold a restart window. I'll coordinate. They prefer we don't touch routing.

Jordan (eng-runtime): ops playbook: 
- don't route new traffic to pool until readiness threshold met
- if readiness failures are identical 5x within 10m, autoscaler should stop spinning up and escalate to oncall

DevOps: adding quick diagnostic snippet for logs search: 
```
index=acme-prod source=pod_logs "fetching config" | stats count by status_code, message
```

Lina (eng-sre): I'm going to open a follow-up incident ticket to track the infra change. Tags: autoscale, readiness-gate, customer-impact. Assigning to Jordan for runtime change, Lina for alerting/console, Alex for customer comms.

Alex (support): ACME notified. They updated the secret and confirmed pods started passing readiness at 09:45. Errors dropped. They want a postmortem and a config-safe rollout recommendation.

Jordan (eng-runtime): plan: land attach-state change behind a feature flag this week, roll to prod next Tues. Also add a health-class metric for "config-fetch-401".

Lina (eng-sre): I'll add an alert: if >3 scale attempts in 10m for same pool + 0% new-ready -> paged oncall.

Maya (customer-success): ACME appreciated the quick turnaround. They're still asking for guarantee this won't recur. I'll share our remediation plan and timelines.

Alex (support): notes for postmortem: customer rotated API key (external service) -> cluster secret stale -> readiness failures -> autoscaler continued scale because capacity reported on node provision not pod readiness -> 503s during surge. Next steps listed above.

autoscaler-bot: incident ticket created: INC-2024-3179 (autoscale-readiness-gate).

Jordan (eng-runtime): putting a short repro PR and unit tests up in the morning. Will @-mention Lina for alert review.

Alex (support): thanks all. I'll close the support thread once postmortem draft ready. :white_check_mark:
